newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain says metals strike turnout was up to 74 pct.
newsitem.headline: Spain says metals strike turnout was up to 74 pct.

text.p: Turnout at Thursday's one-day strikes by metal workers protesting at goverment privatisation plans averaged 74 percent at companies grouped under holding company Agencia Industrial del Estado (AIE), the Industry Ministry said.
AIE controls steel firm Corporacion Siderurgica Integral (CSI).

Turnout at companies grouped under Sociedad Estatal de Participaciones Industriales (SEPI) was lower, at an average of 34.9 percent, the ministry said. SEPI controls alumnium producer Inespal, as well as aerospace firm Construcciones Aeronauticas (CASA).
Unions on Thursday estimated turnout across the country at 85-90 percent of the 50,000 metal sector workers called out.
A particular focus of the stoppage was the plan to sell integrated aluminium producer Inespal to Aluminium Company of America (Alcao).

Employees are also worried about plans to sell steel producer Corporacion Siderurgica Integral (CSI) to a foreign entity. So far the only official bid is from France's Usinor, although other metal firms are thought to be interested.
Strikes at Inespal and CSI alone have been called for July 17 and 24.
